subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable auto-cleanup and archival policy for webhook/hook sessions

question: Should hook sessions remain persistent by default with an explicit per-hook ephemeral/retention mode, or should all hook sessions inherit a new global cleanup policy?
rationale: Current main supports both one-shot generated hook keys and intentionally reusable stable keys, so the default, policy scope, transcript semantics, and interaction with generic maintenance cannot be chosen safely from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Explicit lifecycle per hook
options.body: Keep current persistence as the default and add a mapping/request lifecycle mode for persistent, completion-cleaned, or TTL-cleaned sessions with explicit transcript handling.

options.title: Global hook retention
options.body: Add only a global `hooks.sessionRetention` duration, preserving sessions until the timer expires but leaving immediate disposal and per-mapping intent unsupported.

options.title: Use generic maintenance
options.body: Decline a hook-specific surface and document `session.maintenance` as the supported age/count/disk-budget cleanup mechanism.

recommendation.title: Explicit lifecycle per hook
recommendation.body: Keep current persistence as the default and add a mapping/request lifecycle mode for persistent, completion-cleaned, or TTL-cleaned sessions with explicit transcript handling.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review and broad hook/config history make steipete the strongest available routing candidate for the product-level default and config-surface choice.
